newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Bank of Scotland seeing pay-back.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Bank of Scotland seeing pay-back.

text.p: Bank of Scotland governor Bruce Pattullo on Wednesday said the bank was seeing growth across its business and strongly defended the recent high level of cost growth, saying it was already paying back.
"There's nothing wrong with spending money if you are getting a pay-back," Pattullo told Reuters in an interview. "We think we can afford to invest money. In fact, it would be criminal not to."
The Bank raised pre-tax profits by 24 percent in the first half to 324.3 million stg and paid an 18.8 percent higher dividend of 2.91 pence per share.

The pre-tax profit and dividend figures were better than expected by analysts who had warned that the numbers would be hard to compare with last year becasue they include a first-time contribution, of 38.9 million stg, from the Bank's Australian acquisition BankWest.
Pattullo said the recent rise in costs at the bank had been an historic "quantum leap" which would not always be repeated and had produced a very early and continuing pay-back.

"If you strip out the costs associated with BankWest, costs have gone up 15 percent," Pattullo said. "But net interest income is up 16 percent and non-interest income is up 19 percent. It's that juxtapositioon that's the important thing."
Bank of Scotland's cost to income ratio rose to 52.9 percent compared to 52.1 percent at the end of the last financial year, and would have been 51.3 percent excluding BankWest.
Its tier one capital ratio rose to 6.3 percent from 6.1 percent in February and Pattullo said this was in "remarkably good order."
He pointed to the Bank's ability to generate capital, adding this was also reflected in its dividend increase.

He said the integration of BankWest was proceeding as planned, adding that the bank was suffering from the price battle in the Australian residential mortgage market but is performing better than expected in other areas.
Pattullo said Bank of Scotland has no plans for further major acquisitions describing BankWest as a "once and for all".
In its UK markets, Pattullo said conditions remain competitive in an environment characterised by a surplus of capital coupled with only moderate economic activity.
But he noted that margins in the mortgage market have stabilised and have actually widened in the first half compared to the second six months of the previous year.
